steps: The coordinator gathers willingness to commit.
A pre-commit phase tells participants that unanimous readiness was reached.
Under bounded-delay and failure assumptions, participants use timeout state to progress.

lesson.scenario: A warehouse fleet switches two loading robots to a new route under bounded-delay assumptions.

steps.title: Propose the route
steps.narration: The controller asks whether both robots can safely adopt route R2.
steps.outcome: No robot has crossed the point where it expects a commit.
steps.invariant: A NO reply or expired first-phase deadline causes ABORT.

steps.title: Collect unanimous readiness
steps.narration: Both robots report that route R2 is feasible and reserve their next movement slot.
steps.outcome: The controller may enter the extra pre-commit phase.
steps.invariant: PRE_COMMIT is sent only after unanimous YES replies.

steps.title: Enter pre-commit
steps.narration: Each robot acknowledges PRE_COMMIT, learning that every participant was ready.
steps.outcome: Participants now distinguish unanimous readiness from an uncertain prepare.
steps.invariant: A pre-committed participant must not independently abort.

steps.title: Use the timeout assumption
steps.narration: The controller pauses, but the watchdog confirms the modeled bounded delay rather than a partition.
steps.outcome: Robot Beacon can seek peers and progress only because timing and failure assumptions hold.
steps.invariant: Non-blocking progress is unsafe if a network partition can mimic controller failure.

steps.title: Commit the route change
steps.narration: Recovery establishes that PRE_COMMIT was reached, and both robots activate R2.
steps.outcome: Both robots follow R2; the lesson exposes why real partitions undermine 3PC guarantees.
steps.invariant: Commit safety depends on the stated bounded-delay and no-partition model.

production.scenario: A prepaid-plan activation service coordinates billing and quota updates inside one tightly controlled datacenter fabric.
components: Carrier agents activating prepaid plans for subscribers
Boundary service that validates the requested plan and account
Black-box transaction service for subscriber activation workflows
Authoritative account balance and tariff state
Authoritative data, voice, and SMS entitlements
Durable record of each activation workflow state
Agent that finishes or unwinds incomplete activations after timeouts
flows: A carrier agent asks the platform to activate a prepaid plan for a subscriber.
The activation API creates one workflow that spans billing and quota state.
The coordinator asks billing to stage the new tariff and balance treatment.
The coordinator asks quota storage to stage the matching service entitlements.
The current workflow phase is durably recorded so recovery can continue from a known point.
The recovery agent scans the durable journal for activations that stopped making progress.
If the original coordinator is gone, the recovery agent delivers the durable outcome to billing.
The same recovery path completes or unwinds subscriber entitlements.
